title: Lift a pre-authorization's hold when it is reversed

blocks.text: Hotels and fuel pumps send pre-authorizations (`0100`), and for each one your server places a hold on the cardholder's account. When the stay is cancelled, or the pump never got an answer, the acquirer reverses the pre-authorization with an `0400`, and repeats it as `0401` until it is answered.

The complaints: guests still see a hotel's hold days after the desk cancelled it; one cardholder had the same hold given back twice; and the acquirer's operations team asks why some reversals come back refused.

`ReleaseHold` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ReleaseHold.java` answers those reversals. Its `HoldTable` (at the bottom of the file) is the table the authorization chain fills. Finish `lift` and `answerCode`, marked `TODO`. About seven lines in total.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2, in the test's own JVM, place holds in the table the way the authorization chain would, and send reversals from several terminals.

cases.says: a reversal of a held pre-authorization is answered 0410 with its own STAN and 00
the hold is found through the original's STAN and time in field 90, not the reversal's own, and its amount goes back to the account
a repeated reversal is answered the same way and gives nothing back a second time
a reversal whose original placed no hold is answered 00, since the original has no effect to undo

origin.section: 10.4 A Reversal Is Answered `00`, Finds Its Original Through Field 90, and Undoes It Once

concepts: A reversal finds its original through field 90, undoes it at most once however often it is repeated, and is answered 00 even when there is nothing to undo.
